title: In vivo two-photon calcium imaging of the Drosophila brain
author: Tian, Jiang, et al.

steps.title: Rear flies on standard medium
steps.instruction: Raise flies on standard cornmeal agar medium supplemented with yeast.

steps.title: Maintain flies under controlled conditions
steps.instruction: Keep flies at 24 °C with 60 % humidity on a 12‑hour light/dark cycle.

steps.title: Feed ATR for optogenetics
steps.instruction: For optogenetics experiments, feed adult flies all‑trans‑retinal (ATR) for 3–5 days before imaging.

steps.title: Set up experimental crosses
steps.instruction: Set up crosses and rear experimental and control groups under identical conditions, using age‑matched flies.

steps.title: Check fly genotypes and age
steps.instruction: Consult the key resources table in the paper for the exact genotypes and ages of the flies to be imaged.

steps.title: Preprocess imaging data in Fiji
steps.instruction: Process each recorded TIFF file in Fiji (ImageJ) as follows (≈2 h total).

substeps.instruction: Import the imaging TIFF file into Fiji.
Run Image > Stacks > Z Project to merge the z‑series stack.
Define regions of interest (ROIs) for the target neurons (scale bar = 20 μm).
Save the ROIs in a ZIP file named exactly like the TIFF file.
If the recorded neuron is displaced, correct motion artifacts with the TurboReg plugin.

steps.title: Analyze GCaMP signals in MATLAB
steps.instruction: Load the ROI ZIP file in MATLAB, extract fluorescence traces, and save the results to a MAT file.

steps.title: Plot data and perform statistics
steps.instruction: Import the MAT file into GraphPad Prism 8, plot calcium traces, generate heat maps, and conduct the appropriate statistical analyses (e.g., mean ± SEM).

description: Two-photon calcium imaging of live adult flies provides a more accurate reflection of physiological conditions. The flies were raised on a standard cornmeal agar medium supplemented with yeast. They were maintained at 24°C with 60% humidity under a 12-hour light/dark cycle. For optogenetics experiments coupled with two-photon calcium imaging, the flies were fed all-trans-retinal (ATR) for 3–5 days before imaging. Crosses were set up and reared under identical conditions. Both the experimental and control groups consisted of age-matched flies. Detailed information about the flies, including genotypes and age, is provided in the key resources table in the paper.
